title: POC scoping: model shortlist + multilingual tradeoffs — LumenAI
summary: POC scoping to pick an open-model shortlist for a customer-support assistant in Spanish/Portuguese + English. Discussed success criteria (quality, latency, cost), workload sizing, benchmark plan, and 4-week timeline. Redwood to run latency/cost benchmarks on 3 models and provide quantization recommendations; customer to share 1k labeled eval set and traffic profile.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Priya Nair: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, goals for today are to lock down the POC acceptance criteria and pick a 2-3 model shortlist we can benchmark. quick intro round.
[00:00:18] Marta Gonzales: Hi all, Marta here, Head of NLP at LumenAI. We're building a support assistant for LatAm call center automation — Spanish primary, Portuguese secondary, English fallback. key things are accuracy on slot extraction and helpfulness on follow-ups. latency matters for UI snappiness and cost matters because we'll scale fast.
[00:00:45] Ethan Cole: Great, Ethan from Redwood infra/SE. we'll help size GPU requirements and run microbenchmarks. question: what's your expected concurrency and average request size?
[00:00:58] Devon Reyes: We're expecting peak concurrency around 12–15 agents hitting the assistant concurrently, average prompt + response ~250–400 tokens, sometimes longer for full transcript summarization ~1.2k tokens but that's <5% of traffic.
[00:01:25] Priya Nair: OK that maps to throughput needs. for the POC let's define an SLO for latency: p95 generation latency under 400ms for typical 300-token exchanges, and cost-per-1k-tokens under a target — do you have a cost target?
[00:01:43] Samir Kapoor: We'd like to see numbers to decide, but initial target is under $0.020 per 1k tokens end-to-end if possible. that's negotiable if quality is significantly better.
[00:01:56] Helena Ortiz: Also must support Spanish PL-ES and Brazilian PT-BR idioms; our error tolerance is low on policy/deflection cases. We'll provide a labeled eval set of ~1k examples including transcripts and expected extractions.
[00:02:14] Ethan Cole: Perfect. On model choices for open-source, we've seen the usual tradeoffs. My initial shortlist: Llama-2-13B (13B), Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Falcon-40B-Instruct-lite or a quantized Falcon 40B variant. But given multilingual focus, we should also consider MosaicML's Mixed-language models or a smaller specialized model like OpenAssistant variants.
[00:02:42] Marta Gonzales: Quick interjection: our previous internal test found Llama-2 okay on English but lags on PT-BR idiomatic phrases. We leaned toward Mistral for cost but not sure on PT-BR.
[00:02:56] Ethan Cole: Right, that's common. Mistral tends to be strong in European languages but less tuned for Latin American Spanish. Falcon and Llama families have mixed results; quantization (4-bit) helps cost but can drop certain token-level exact-match metrics.
[00:03:15] Priya Nair: for the POC we recommend benchmarking three variants: (1) Llama-2-13B 8-bit quantized, (2) Mistral-7B-Instruct 4-bit quantized, and (3) Falcon-40B 8-bit or an instruction-tuned 16-bit run as a control. we'll also throw in a distilled or instruction-tuned OA (OpenAssistant) variant if you want a smaller footprint candidate.
[00:03:37] Samir Kapoor: Good. How do we measure "quality" for acceptance? exact-match on slots, F1 for extraction, and a human-rated helpfulness score?
[00:03:45] Priya Nair: yes — we'll use your 1k labeled set for automated metrics: slot F1, intent accuracy, and a synthetic BLEU/ROUGE for canned replies. plus blind human eval on 200 samples rated 1–5 for helpfulness and safety. acceptance threshold suggested: slot F1 >= 0.88, intent accuracy >= 0.93, and median helpfulness >= 4.0. are those realistic?
[00:04:10] Marta Gonzales: 0.88 F1 is ambitious but reasonable for us. if latency/cost tradeoffs are manageable we can accept a small drop.
[00:04:19] Devon Reyes: also need to test streaming vs non-streaming. UI expects partial tokens to show within 150–200ms; can Redwood simulate streaming latency?
[00:04:28] Ethan Cole: yes we can run streaming benchmarks and measure time-to-first-token. we typically test time-to-first-token, p50/p95 generation, and end-to-end time including network RTT to your region. we'll simulate a Rio de Janeiro cloud region — current infra is in us-east but we can model region RTT.
[00:04:49] Helena Ortiz: Security note — data residency: some Spanish transcripts contain PII; we need to know log retention on Redwood hosted and Dedicated options.
[00:04:58] Priya Nair: Redwood Dedicated or Private are options. for hosted POC we can enable no-log mode and sign an NDA; Dedicated gives you control over retention. we'll share SOC2 and our retention docs after the call.
[00:05:12] Samir Kapoor: timeline? we're hoping to run a 4-week POC with a final decision after. can Redwood deliver bench results in one week?
[00:05:20] Ethan Cole: Yes — if you share the eval set and a traffic sample today we can run latency and quality runs in ~5 business days. we will provide cost estimates per 1M tokens for each model and quantization profile.
[00:05:34] Marta Gonzales: Great. On the workload sizing, we need to be explicit: 15 peak concurrency, average 350 tokens, 5% long-form summarization at 1.2k tokens. That will affect batching and KV-cache strategy.
[00:05:50] Marcos Liu: Note — for summarization we often route to a heavier model variant or a separate summarization pipeline to keep latency on short-turn exchanges. we can configure policy-based routing in Redwood to send heavy requests to a different pool.
[00:06:05] Devon Reyes: How about quantization stability? in the past 4-bit runs gave hallucination spikes on slot boundaries.
[00:06:12] Ethan Cole: Good point. part of the benchmark will measure hallucination/error modes: exact-match dropoff at token boundaries and consistency across repeats. we also run evals with temperature 0 and 0.2 to emulate deterministic extraction.
[00:06:29] Priya Nair: Let's capture acceptance criteria again — quality thresholds, latency SLO p95 <400ms typical, time-to-first-token <200ms for streaming, and cost thresholds. We'll make those concrete in the POC plan doc.
[00:06:42] Samir Kapoor: Can you summarize the three models and why each is included?
[00:06:48] Ethan Cole: Sure: Llama-2-13B 8-bit — good balance of capability and footprint; customizable and known behavior on English/Spanish with instruction tuning. Mistral-7B-Instruct 4-bit — lower cost, strong instruction following, generally fast; risk is PT-BR gaps. Falcon-40B 8/16-bit — higher quality ceiling for hard cases and long-context summarization, but much higher cost. optional: OA-distilled 3–7B as a cheap baseline.
[00:07:16] Marta Gonzales: Ok we want Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B, and Falcon-40B as the three. include OA-distil as a baseline.
[00:07:23] Priya Nair: Good. Bench plan: Redwood will run accuracy on your 1k eval set, run synthetic load for latency at concurrency 1/5/15 with your token distributions, run streaming TTF tests, and costing. We'll deliver a report with metrics and recommended quantization and a short runbook for production rollout.
[00:07:44] Helena Ortiz: For the human eval, will Redwood recruit raters or do we run internally?
[00:07:49] Ethan Cole: We can do both; common approach is Redwood runs a 200-sample blind panel and you run an internal QA pass. we'll compare.
[00:07:59] Samir Kapoor: Any mention of competitors or other vendors? we looked at Anthropic Claude and OpenAI but want to prioritize open models for cost control.
[00:08:09] Priya Nair: Noted — we'll include a short appendix comparing the best-in-class closed APIs so you can see the cost/latency delta.
[00:08:16] Marta Gonzales: Data handling — we need KMS integration and audit logs for the POC if possible.
[00:08:22] Priya Nair: We'll include KMS options for Dedicated/Private and show hosted no-log options. audit logs are available on Dedicated.
[00:08:30] Devon Reyes: Another operational ask — can Redwood run a small A/B against our current rule-based assistant to show delta on deflection?
[00:08:36] Marcos Liu: We can run A/B if you can route a portion of traffic; for the POC we usually do offline evals and a short live test if you permit.
[00:08:47] Samir Kapoor: OK next steps?
[00:08:50] Priya Nair: We'll summarize — action items and who owns them. Redwood to run bench plan for the four model candidates, deliver report in 5 business days. LumenAI to provide 1k labeled eval set, traffic profile, and CRM details. We'll also add security docs and an optional pricing estimate for Dedicated.
[00:09:10] Marta Gonzales: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[00:09:15] (call ends)

Notes: transcription has minor errors: e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache" appears in rough notes; speaker labels sometimes merge in exported file but corrected above.
